purpose: R2A, R3b-1, FC-1, R2b-3, R3c1 and R2 attempt/tool-durable runtime evidence. T01-T18 retain typed-terminal ownership; F01-F05 pin mailbox drain and dependency direction; FC01 pins the migration join; U01-U07 pin the Step-scoped durable failure settlement; Q01-Q12 pin the private bounded mailbox-advisory seam; TD01-TD28 pin governed tool execution, durable terminal truth, bounded coalescing/retry, sealed attempt admission, pre-commit call-limit refusal, and provider-failure task abort; PA01-PA12 pin the private physical-attempt owner. SE01 pins the L4a rule that a finish normalizing to a failure is classified before the attempt terminal is written, never after. Each entry names one load-bearing behaviour, the exact source edit that removes it, and the witness that must turn red once it is gone. SE05-SE06 pin L4a's durable half: the success terminal's dispatch to the store seam, and the write boundary's refusal of a failure-shaped finish. IGP01-IGP13 pin the U2 attempt vertical: custody deletion, both settlement halves, the visible-output retry guard, fabricated success from a forwarded provider failure, unbounded-channel resurrection, tool-terminal durable-write deletion, settle-before-terminal reorder, the opener's configured-route independence, post-custody refusal custody return, the single-transaction reserve-and-permit, the positional opening law, and the pre-stream typed-failure class.
isolation: Every mutation is applied inside its own disposable git worktree checked out at the exact candidate commit. No mutant is ever written into the calling worktree, so a restore step cannot silently leave a stale build behind.
scope_note: T01-T18 and F01-F05 remain accounted in their existing residuals; FC01 remains the join-only migration law. U01 replaces the provisional StepFailed path, U02/U03 pin one pre-provider authority read, U04 keeps election out of terminal settlement, U05 preserves the accepted typed reason, U06 suppresses duplicate advisory on idempotent replay, and U07 pins the reviewed direct event dependency. Q01-Q12 pin exact private SEMADV1 metadata, UTF-8 byte accounting, independent key/byte caps, reserved sticky rescan, same-key phase convergence, durable ordering, sink-loss isolation, and durable-reread reconnect. PA01-PA12 use the fresh whole-token PA allocation: one injected mint and ceiling, reserve then durable permit before one private opener, fail-closed public composition, durable recovery classification, existing atomic process-loss settlement, distinct retry identities, and sealed public surfaces. Crash rollback remains carried by the accepted store chokepoint and its named R2b-2 witnesses rather than a fabricated runtime mutation row; R3c1 source-cursor, source-ack, ProtocolVersion, public wire, client, and transport remain explicit residuals in R2B3_RESIDUALS.md and R3C1_RESIDUALS.md. SE01 belongs to L4a and guards the attempt terminal arm only: ContentFilter and Error are the two oracle finishes that normalize to NormalizedFinish::Failed, and the arm that used to build the success terminal from the raw finish now classifies first. The workspace's other normalization (application.rs) reads report.result, which the Step driver returns only after committing the Step terminal, so it cannot carry this law; that is why the row targets the attempt arm and not the routing gate. SE05 and SE06 are the same lane's durable half: SE05 pins that the success terminal is dispatched to the store seam rather than delegated to the in-memory owner, and SE06 pins that the write boundary refuses a failure-shaped finish rather than encoding it as a disposition. SE01 and SE06 are deliberately the same rule at its two ends - classify before settling, and refuse to write what was not classified - because a rule stated at one end only leaves one place to get it wrong. IGP01-IGP13 use the whole-token IGP allocation, which a fresh recursive census over every manifest in this workspace confirms this manifest owns alone. IGP12 is the U2-ETA-R1-F1 correction's row and its anchor sits on the opening DECISION; IGP05 was re-anchored onto the POST-OPENING forward at the same time, so the two rows cannot reach each other's code: IGP05 can no longer touch the synthetic first-fragment refusal, and IGP12's mutant is the pre-correction permissive shape rather than a guard deletion, because the defect that was removed was tolerance of a first fragment that is not AttemptOpened. Both halves of IGP12's witness were shown to fail on their own: the permissive shape kills case 1, and a separate swallow-later-openings shape kills case 2 while case 1 still passes, so neither case is carrying the other. IGP13 is the U2-ETA-R1-F2 correction's row and the only cross-crate IGP entry: it mutates the provider's staged-Codex reader, whose law is observable only from the runtime that consumes it, so the row names the runtime package its witness lives in. Its mutant restores the pre-correction shape â€” the failure yielded with no opening marker ahead of it â€” rather than deleting a guard, because the defect removed was a MISSING emission. No existing row owned this law: IGP09 owns the endpoint's configured route identity and IGP10 owns custody return on a post-custody refusal, and IGP05 owns the POST-opening forward, which a pre-stream failure never reaches. The wrapper loops rather than awaiting the second fragment inside the opening arm: a direct await there would let the first content fragment bypass the single post-opening forward, which is IGP05's anchor, and IGP05 would survive its own mutant (the F2 mutation audit).

mutations.law: A finish that normalizes to a failure never settles as an ending: the attempt terminal is classified before it is written, not after
The Step SUCCESS terminal is dispatched to the durable store seam, not delegated to the in-memory inner owner: a Step that succeeds writes a durable fact rather than one that dies with the process

The durability boundary refuses a failure-shaped finish instead of encoding it as a disposition: a content-policy refusal never becomes a durable success terminal, stated at the write end as well as at the attempt arm

Custody deletion: the custody the opener yielded is HELD in the ledger from reserve until its receipt settles; a source that drops it at prepare leaves the reserved receipt unsettleable and the hold count witnesses it
A clean Step terminal settles every reserved attempt receipt INSIDE its own transaction; deleting the success-half settlement leaves the durable receipt standing and custody held after the Step ended
Error and cancellation terminals settle receipts too: deleting the failure-half settlement leaves the failed attempt's durable receipt standing after the Step failed
visible-output-no-retry: a retryable provider failure AFTER visible output fails the Step with no second provider call; deleting the guard retries into the queued second response

Raw-FinishReason resurrection on the POST-OPENING forward: once the opening decision is made every later fragment passes through untouched, so the production reader cannot fabricate a success terminal from a provider failure; rewriting a forwarded ProviderFailure into ProviderTerminal(Stop) turns a retryable failure into a one-attempt clean end and the retry witness refuses it. Anchored past the opening decision on purpose, so it cannot reach the synthetic first-fragment refusal that IGP12 owns
Unbounded-channel resurrection: an unbounded queue constructor reappearing beside the bounded provider handoff is caught by the architecture gate
Tool terminals are durable facts written before the Step terminal; routing them to the in-memory owner erases the durable rows and their committed advisories
Receipts settle AFTER the terminal append inside one transaction, proven by terminal read-back; settling before the append cannot prove the terminal and the clean vertical refuses it

The endpoint's route is the opener's CONFIGURED identity, independent of the target; re-deriving it from the target makes EndpointServesAnotherRoute a comparison of a value with itself and the wrong-route witness refuses it
Custody survives every post-custody refusal: a transport failure after from_carrier returns the custody inside its refusal, and a mutant that destroys it is refused by the post-custody witness

Reserve and send permit are ONE transaction: a permit refusal after the reserve rolls the reservation back, so no durable receipt survives an admission-refused Step; a mutant that splits the commit leaves the reserved receipt behind and the permit-refusal witness refuses it

Opening suppression is POSITIONAL, never first-sighting: the first inner fragment MUST be AttemptOpened, and anything else there means the stream never opened, which outranks whatever class it claimed. A permissive first fragment lets an unopened stream settle as a clean Stop, because the supervisor opens the validator itself and nothing downstream can notice the adapter's opening never arrived

A failure that arrives BEFORE any stream fragment keeps the adapter's OWN typed class. The staged Codex arm must yield AttemptOpened first and hand its typed ProviderFailure over unchanged, because the consumer's opening law is positional: a failure arriving at position one is refused as InvalidProviderOutput, which overwrites the real class and with it retry eligibility, so a 429 or a transport drop would arrive terminal and never be retried
A request-sent receipt recovered after process loss is settled through the store's exact preallocated ProcessLoss terminal; skipping settlement cannot advance into reclaim or provider replay
Resurrection closure: after proving or appending the exact terminal, recovery reclaims the live receipt so a later restart has no attempt to resurrect
An untrustworthy receipt is moved to durable quarantine before the recovery cursor advances; it is never skipped into absence or given a fabricated terminal
Acceptance-corpus counterexample: executing process-loss recovery has no provider boundary, so a runner that records a second provider call must disagree with the pinned no-replay outcome

Acceptance-corpus resurrection: the second recovery observation must report the exact durable terminal count unchanged; inflating only the later observation to two terminals must redden the semantic comparison
